title: Interpolated compatibility matrix refactor and tooling synchronization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Refactor the fallback compatibility matrix to an interpolated, normalized representation that captures tokenizer equivalence, context/sequence-length contract, and tooling (KV cache, runtime flags, CLI versions) compatibility across model variants used by the smart routing system (region selection + tier routing + fallback flows).

Scope: 1) Data model change for the compatibility matrix to enable incremental signals from automated tests and runtime telemetry. 2) Update tooling checkers (tokenizer smoke tests, KV serialization validator, cache format checker) to produce normalized scores. 3) Wire matrix outputs into routing policy decision logic so the router can prefer compatible fallback variants when latency/cost constraints trigger failover. 4) Add CI gates and scheduled sweeps to detect drift.

Out of scope: full re-implementation of serving runtime or kernel selection, and wholesale model conversion. This is focused on compatibility metadata and tooling that verifies runtime interchangeability for fallback decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Compatibility matrix schema version v2 published in the metadata store and documented in Confluence.
A2: Tokenizer equivalence check implemented with a test set; per-variant score persisted and >= 99.8% for all shipping fallback variants or flagged in the matrix.
A3: KV cache serialization/roundtrip validator added with pass/fail and normalized score persisted.
A4: Routing logic updated to consume matrix scores and prefer fallbacks with combined compatibility score >= 0.95 when available.
A5: CI job added that fails for new PRs if a change reduces compatibility score for any fallback variant by >0.5%.
A6: Runbook updated with rollback and manual override steps; doc link added to attachments.
A7: Dashboard tile in Console shows per-variant compatibility trend for the last 30 days.
tasks: T1: Design new matrix schema (columns: tokenizer_hash, tokenizer_score, context_contract, kv_roundtrip_score, tooling_version_range, last_validated_at)
T2: Implement tokenizer smoke harness that runs 15k prompt pairs and produces equivalence ratio
T3: Implement KV roundtrip validator for quantized/8-bit checkpoints
T4: Add matrix writer in metadata service and migration script for existing matrix->v2
T5: Update smart-routing policy code to consult matrix and apply threshold logic
T6: Add CI integration and pre-merge check in GitHub actions
T7: Create Console dashboard tile and wire metrics (compat_score, failing_checks)
T8: Draft runbook and QA checklist for SRE on rollout
decisions: D1: Use a normalized floating compatibility score (0.0-1.0) combining tokenizer, context, and KV checks with weights 0.5/0.3/0.2 respectively.
D2: Matrix storage will be sharded by model family and region to support regional fallbacks and faster lookups in routing path.
D3: CI tolerance for new PRs will be conservative: any drop >0.5% triggers a required reviewer tag from search-and-serve owners.
D4: Routing will prefer variants that meet compatibility >= 0.95; if none, fallback to the highest-scoring variant with explicit SLO-exempt flag and telemetry alerting enabled.
tradeoffs: T-O1: Weighting tokenizer higher (0.5) reduces false-positive compatibility cases but increases maintenance burden when tokenizer tokenizers change.
T-O2: Sharding matrix by region improves latency for routing but increases migration complexity and storage overhead.
T-O3: Adding strict CI gates reduces regression risk but may slow on-call fixes or model onboarding velocity.

risk: Primary risk is false-compatibility assertions: matrix indicates compatibility but runtime subtle differences (tokenizer edge-cases, KV cache format nuances) produce semantic regressions in downstream apps.
mitigation: Mitigations include conservative scoring weights, staged rollout (canary routing to 2% of traffic), telemetry alerting on model fallback error rates, and quick manual override in Console. Also scheduled monthly automated cross-variant regression runs using representative production prompts.
